title: Centralize build toolchain upgrades; add cache observability & layer profiling
creator: Noah Chen
description: Goal: Reduce developer wait time and flakiness by centralizing our approach to build tool upgrades (linters, formatters, compiler toolchains) and surface transparent cache metrics for everyone using the CI. Scope: (1) Create a single upgrade pipeline that stages upgrades across language toolchains (Go, Python, JS) with automated compatibility checks; (2) Add buildkit layer profiling and cache hit/miss metrics into the Redwood Console so engineers can identify expensive layers and low-hit caches; (3) Small image hygiene pass to remove redundant runtime deps and reduce average image size by ~15%. Deliverables: upgrade-pipeline scripts, a build profiling dashboard, a Canary rollout plan for base-image updates, PR templates, and a post-mortem checklist. Acceptance criteria: pipeline runs automatically on new tool releases, profiling metrics are available in the Console for at least 90% of CI jobs, and average cold-cache build time reduced by 20% in the experimental cohort. Rollout notes: start with infra repos -> platform -> services. Backwards compatible: current job YAMLs remain valid; we add opt-in flags initially.
comments: 2025-11-03 -- Noah Chen: Created ticket after spike with Platform where we observed 40% of CI time spent in three heavyweight npm installs. Proposed central pipeline + profiling. Added initial acceptance criteria.

2025-11-06 -- Aisha Patel: Spike complete. Findings: (a) Go toolchain upgrades are low-risk but require pinned module curation; (b) Python venv setup is the biggest cold-cache contributor; (c) buildkit --trace enabled gives useful layer timing with minimal overhead. Recommend implementing a small profiling sidecar to emit layer timings to our metrics pipeline.

2025-11-11 -- Miguel Ortega (infra): WIP PR draft: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9842 adds buildkit trace extraction and a lightweight uploader. Early tests show cache-hit rate metric can be derived reliably for npm and pip steps.

2025-11-14 -- Design review (Lena Park): Suggested dashboard mocks for Console that show per-repo layer breakdown, top 10 cache-miss commands, and a remediation link to the upgrade playbook. Added to project board.

2025-11-17 -- Aisha Patel: Implemented central upgrade pipeline prototype. It creates a branch, runs compatibility matrix job, and opens PR(s) with suggested dependency bumps. Next: wire in canary gating to prevent mass breakage.

2025-11-20 -- QA (Jordan Kim): Found flakes when the pipeline ran simultaneous upgrades across >5 repos due to shared ephemeral artifact store limits. Mitigation: staggered scheduling and local cache warming. Filed followup ENG-87909 to address artifact-store throttling.

2025-11-22 -- Aisha Patel: Canary rollout plan drafted: stage to infra repos (10% of CI runners pinned to new base images), monitor build time & failure rate for 48h, then increase to platform repos. Dashboard alerts configured for >10% failure delta or >15% build time regression.

2025-11-24 -- Noah Chen: Merged initial profiling agent to staging: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9842 merged. Metrics pipeline shows first real data (see Console: /dashboards/ci-build-profiling). Early signal: node_modules installs are 55% of layer time for web-service repo. Next steps: create remediation guidance and prioritize image hygiene PRs.
